coachFit.scope: A well-suited versus poorly suited coach on the same roster; similar fits may be much closer. No universal ranking or required V05 delta.

reserveUpgrade.scope: A clear reserve upgrade, provisional until selected records are checked; V04 is the proposed example, not yet a firm numeric gate.

influenceExpectations.interpretation: Contextual design expectations, not fixed bonuses or independently additive effects.

rosters.name: Your Brunson-Towns-Duncan team
rosters.strength: Three complementary scoring options, a defensive anchor and usable shooting.
rosters.weakness: Early-career Brooks and modest bench support; three scorers must share possessions.
rosters.selectionStory: User-provided completed draft; the anchor for credible qualification contention.
rosters.exposure: Previously measured and used for the season-3 adjustment; never a fresh validation case.

rosters.name: Shaq and Kobe with support
rosters.strength: Dominant inside-out scoring with low-demand perimeter support.
rosters.weakness: Limited secondary creation and a modest reserve.
rosters.selectionStory: Two headline picks followed by familiar championship role players.

rosters.name: Jordan with specialists
rosters.strength: An elite perimeter scorer with playmaking, defensive support and a stretch center.
rosters.weakness: Heavy dependence on Jordan for difficult scoring.
rosters.selectionStory: One marquee star, then deliberately complementary picks.

rosters.name: Detroit collective defense
rosters.strength: Five compatible roles, defensive coverage and a dependable lead guard.
rosters.weakness: Less individual scoring dominance than the exceptional group.
rosters.selectionStory: A recognizable team identity; repeated Detroit rolls may be rare. These are franchise-decade peaks, not one historical season.

rosters.name: Nash and Dirk spacing
rosters.strength: Elite orchestration, shooting and an interior connector.
rosters.weakness: Perimeter defense and no dominant rim protector.
rosters.selectionStory: A playmaker and scoring big followed by shooting and defensive support.

rosters.name: Paul and Garnett two-way fit
rosters.strength: A lead creator, off-ball shooting and versatile defenders.
rosters.weakness: Relies on Paul and Garnett for most self-created offense.
rosters.selectionStory: Users pair a top point guard with a two-way big and fill defensive roles.

rosters.name: LeBron with shooting and support
rosters.strength: An elite offensive hub with shooting and secondary decision-making.
rosters.weakness: No dominant interior scorer; a large burden on LeBron.
rosters.selectionStory: An iconic first pick followed by players who can contribute without dominating the ball.

rosters.name: Curry motion and rim support
rosters.strength: Off-ball shooting, passing and defensive support around Curry.
rosters.weakness: Less high-volume wing creation than the Durant variant.
rosters.selectionStory: A familiar Warriors-style core with a center and reserve chosen for fit.

rosters.name: Magic and Kareem with one shooter
rosters.strength: Elite passing and interior scoring, plus a dedicated perimeter threat.
rosters.weakness: Limited shooting outside Miller and an older reserve guard.
rosters.selectionStory: Traditional stars should remain useful with deliberate shooting support.

rosters.name: Payton and Kemp with Ewing
rosters.strength: Two-way guard play, a shooting wing and strong interior options.
rosters.weakness: Two interior scorers share space and possessions.
rosters.selectionStory: Recognizable Seattle-era picks supplemented by a center; OKC is the dataset's Seattle franchise identity.

rosters.name: Jokic passing hub
rosters.strength: A passing center with a perimeter partner, cutters and defensive wings.
rosters.weakness: No second dominant interior defender in the starting five.
rosters.selectionStory: An iconic hub with several attainable-looking supporting roles, not five MVPs.

rosters.name: Boston wing depth
rosters.strength: Multiple capable scorers, shooting and defensive coverage without a single indispensable role.
rosters.weakness: Older centers and less singular offensive dominance than the exceptional group.
rosters.selectionStory: A recognizable modern team identity; repeated franchise rolls are an accessibility question.

rosters.name: Durant motion superteam
rosters.strength: Elite shooting and creation with passing, rim support and a strong sixth man.
rosters.weakness: Usage sharing and reserve opportunity cost still matter.
rosters.selectionStory: An exceptional ceiling case, not an ordinary obtainable draft.

rosters.name: All-time inside-out balance
rosters.strength: Elite creation, a dominant center and defensive versatility.
rosters.weakness: Several stars must reduce individual possession demands; not unlimited shooting.
rosters.selectionStory: Tests whether extraordinary but role-compatible talent retains exceptional value.

rosters.name: Jordan-Bird with twin anchors
rosters.strength: Passing, perimeter shot creation and two elite interior defenders.
rosters.weakness: Frontcourt overlap and high aggregate usage; historical shooting volume differs from modern teams.
rosters.selectionStory: A ceiling test for complementary historical greatness rather than modern shooting alone.

rosters.name: Shooting around Hakeem
rosters.strength: Elite spacing and orchestration around a two-way center.
rosters.weakness: Perimeter defense and several high-demand offensive options.
rosters.selectionStory: An offensive ceiling roster that still invests in a defensive anchor.

rosters.name: Magic's two-big all-time team
rosters.strength: Elite passing, interior talent and perimeter defense with a dedicated shooter.
rosters.weakness: Only one high-volume starting shooter and two interior scorers.
rosters.selectionStory: Tests an exceptional traditional lineup without making every starter a shooter.

rosters.name: LeBron-Jokic shared creation
rosters.strength: Exceptional passing, scoring and defensive support.
rosters.weakness: Overlapping creators and usage sharing; no automatic perfect-season expectation.
rosters.selectionStory: An exceptional multi-hub roster, reserved alongside the simpler passing-big family.

rosters.name: Every scorer wants the ball
rosters.strength: Overwhelming individual scoring talent.
rosters.weakness: Extreme possession overlap, uneven defense and a high-demand reserve.
rosters.selectionStory: A plausible famous-name instinct; should expose fit costs without assuming great players become worthless.

rosters.name: Offense without defensive coverage
rosters.strength: Creation, shooting and scoring at every position.
rosters.weakness: Limited defensive coverage, overlapping scorers and bench usage.
rosters.selectionStory: Users prioritize recognizable offensive talent at every pick.

rosters.name: Defense with no shooting outlet
rosters.strength: Passing, rebounding and substantial defensive talent.
rosters.weakness: Very limited shooting and too many starters who need space near the basket.
rosters.selectionStory: A user overcorrects toward defense around one perimeter scorer.

rosters.name: Familiar names, wrong career versions
rosters.strength: Recognizable names and some retained skill.
rosters.weakness: These are late-career franchise records, not prime versions; confirm the stored talent supports the provisional 30-40 target before simulation.
rosters.selectionStory: A novice recognizes the names but misses the version labels. Selected-version talent, not reputation, should determine team strength.

rosters.name: All support, no scoring lead
rosters.strength: Defense, rebounding and low-demand support roles.
rosters.weakness: No proven high-volume offensive lead; this is a negative control, not a contender.
rosters.selectionStory: Tests whether chemistry bonuses can incorrectly substitute for scoring talent.

rosters.name: Historical greatness, crowded frontcourt
rosters.strength: Exceptional historical talent, defense and rebounding.
rosters.weakness: Redundant frontcourt roles, little perimeter shooting and an expensive reserve role.
rosters.selectionStory: User approved exceptional status: extraordinary selected-version talent should outweigh spacing and positional overlap on this team.

variants.name: Later Brooks
variants.rationale: Do not assume the later version is better in every respect; inspect the whole-player tradeoff before assigning a direction.

variants.name: Trade wing shooting for rebounding
variants.rationale: Less shooting but more rebounding and defense; review the acceptable cost before setting a numeric delta.

variants.name: Remove the lead scorer
variants.rationale: Removing Jordan should not be rewarded merely for lowering usage.

variants.name: More capable reserve big
variants.expectation: Clear reserve upgrade should add roughly 2-4 expected wins, provisional
variants.rationale: Confirm the selected records make this a clear upgrade before applying the range; higher historical usage should not automatically make a better reserve harmful.

variants.name: Popovich instead of Sloan
variants.rationale: Measure a coach change on the same players; do not assume a universal coach ranking.

variants.name: Swap Duncan and Towns slots
variants.rationale: Both assignments are legal; the shared PF/C anchor calculation should not depend on which big occupies which of these two slots.

variants.name: Young Kobe instead of prime Kobe
variants.expectation: Weaker if stored records confirm the talent gap
variants.rationale: Career versions should matter; lower usage alone should not turn a confirmed talent loss into an upgrade.

variants.name: Manu instead of Fisher off the bench
variants.expectation: Improvement if stored records confirm a clear upgrade
variants.rationale: Account for team fit without automatically penalizing a better reserve for higher historical usage; no fixed name-based bonus.

reviewDecisions: 1: F06 exceptional, 69-74; greatness outweighs awkward fit on this roster.
2: F04 below .500, 30-40 provisionally; check selected career records before freezing the target.
3: F05 below .500, 35-44; defense matters but cannot replace an offensive lead.
4: F01 strong contender, 64-68; stars can share possessions despite overlap.
5: C03 strong contender, 64-68; Jordan with capable support should usually qualify.
6: C04 strong contender, 64-68; collective defense and credible offense provide another route.
7: F03 qualification contender, 59-63; creation and defense compensate partly for limited shooting.
8: F02 qualification contender, 59-63; elite offense compensates partly for defensive weaknesses.
9: Retain C01 at 59-63 and C02/C05-C12 at 64-68, including their proposed coaches and reserves.
10: Retain E01-E06 at 69-74; a shared band does not require identical results or rankings.
11: Coach fit contrast roughly 2-4 expected wins; similar fits may be closer, with no universal best coach.
12: Clear reserve upgrade roughly 2-4 expected wins provisionally; confirm V04 player records first.
13: Approve remaining comparison rules; conditional record checks remain, with no invented numeric delta for every substitution.
evaluationConstraints: Expectation-setting only; no authorization to simulate, tune or change live rules in this review step.
Stable roster IDs retain their original prefixes; group and tier fields, not prefixes, define current classifications.
Keep the existing 15 development and 9 validation rosters and their family assignments; future variants inherit parent reservations.
Check F04 and conditional substitutions against stored player records without using benchmark performance to choose expectations.
Qualification probabilities are reporting requirements, not approved universal bands; numerical gates for qualitative comparisons remain unspecified.
Evaluate roll and coach-offer accessibility separately; legal placement is not proof of an obtainable draft history.
